_: THE NAMED-INDICATOR LIBRARY. One entry per named indicator: the ONE checked formula the assistant builds when a member names it (api/services/named_indicators.py says how). A person writes `formula` (with {param} where a parameter's number goes), `params`, `aliases` and `evidence`; tools/named_indicators_build.py writes `tree`, `sites` and each newest version's `maths`. THE RULE: an entry's maths never changes under the same version; a change is a new entry in its `versions` with the reason. `evidence.published` is what was READ, on the date in `read`, at the pages listed; `says` is the definition in those pages' terms. Aliases are never a bare two- or three-letter acronym. `held` lists names UCT knows and has NO checked formula for: each is refused by name with the way forward (`describe` is the rule in plain words, an example of what the member can ask for instead).

outputs.label: KAMA
outputs.formula: accum(close, self + pow(abs(close - close[{er_length}]) / sum(abs(close - close[1]), {er_length}) * (2 / ({fast} + 1) - 2 / ({slow} + 1)) + 2 / ({slow} + 1), 2) * (close - self), 300)

sources.title: StockCharts ChartSchool: Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA)
TradingView help center: Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA)

published.says: ER = |close - close 10 ago| / sum of |close - prior close| over 10; SC = (ER x (2/(2+1) - 2/(30+1)) + 2/(30+1)) squared; KAMA = prior KAMA + SC x (price - prior KAMA). Settings 10, 2, 30.
published.note: StockCharts starts the series from a simple average; UCT starts it from the close 300 bars back on every bar.

published.says: MD = prior MD + (price - prior MD) / (N x (price / prior MD) to the 4th power).
published.note: A variant divides by 0.6 x N. Which constant McGinley first published was not confirmed on a page read; this is TradingView's documented form. Its default length, 14, was read back from TradingView's own settings.

capture.detail: TradingView's line IS this formula carried from the mean of the first 14 closes: equal on all 8,495 and all 654 bars when carried that way. UCT restarts it 300 bars back on every bar: within 3 billionths on SPY (8 bars differ at all), within 0.015% on RDDT, a young stock in a long rise, where the line is slow to forget its start.

outputs.label: Connors RSI
outputs.formula: (rsi(close, {rsi_length}) + rsi(accum(0, close > close[1] ? (self > 0 ? self + 1 : 1) : close < close[1] ? (self < 0 ? self - 1 : -1) : 0, 100), {streak_length}) + percentrank(roc(close, 1), {rank_length})) / 3

sources.title: An Introduction to ConnorsRSI (Connors Research Trading Strategy Series, 2012)

published.says: ConnorsRSI(3,2,100) = [RSI(close,3) + RSI(streak,2) + PercentRank(100)] / 3. The streak counts consecutive up closes (positive) or down closes (negative) and is 0 on an unchanged close. PercentRank is the share of the previous 100 one-day returns that are less than today's.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar after bar 130 on both charts. Bars 102 to 130 differ: the streak is first known 100 bars in, and its 2-bar RSI needs a few bars more.

published.says: Long = 22-day highest high - ATR(22) x 3; short = 22-day lowest low + ATR(22) x 3.
published.note: TradingView gives the lookback and the ATR their own lengths (both 22); so does this entry.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar after bar 355. Earlier bars differ by an amount that shrinks every bar (2% at bar 27, under a millionth of a percent by bar 355): UCT's ATR is Wilder's original and TradingView's is seeded one bar earlier.

outputs.label: Chaikin Money Flow
outputs.formula: sum(high == low ? 0 : ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume, {length}) / sum(volume, {length})

sources.title: TradingView help center: Chaikin Money Flow (CMF)

published.says: Money flow multiplier = [(close - low) - (high - close)] / (high - low); money flow volume = multiplier x volume; CMF = 20-period sum of money flow volume / 20-period sum of volume.
published.note: A bar with no range (high equals low) has no multiplier in the published formula; it counts as 0 here.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for.

outputs.label: Ultimate Oscillator
outputs.formula: 100 * (4 * sum(close - min(low, close[1]), {fast}) / sum(max(high, close[1]) - min(low, close[1]), {fast}) + 2 * sum(close - min(low, close[1]), {middle}) / sum(max(high, close[1]) - min(low, close[1]), {middle}) + sum(close - min(low, close[1]), {slow}) / sum(max(high, close[1]) - min(low, close[1]), {slow})) / 7

published.says: BP = close - min(low, prior close); TR = max(high, prior close) - min(low, prior close); average N = sum of BP / sum of TR for N = 7, 14, 28; UO = 100 x (4 x avg7 + 2 x avg14 + avg28) / 7.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for.

published.says: AO = SMA of (high + low) / 2 over 5 - SMA of (high + low) / 2 over 34.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for.

published.says: Coppock = 10-period weighted average of (14-period rate of change + 11-period rate of change).
published.note: Designed for monthly bars; it computes on whatever bars the chart shows.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for.

published.says: PC = close - prior close; TSI = 100 x (13-period EMA of the 25-period EMA of PC) / (13-period EMA of the 25-period EMA of |PC|).
published.note: No signal line: the sources read do not agree on its length.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for. TradingView also draws a 13-bar signal line; this entry has none.

outputs.label: VI+
outputs.formula: sum(abs(high - low[1]), {length}) / sum(max(high - low, max(abs(high - close[1]), abs(low - close[1]))), {length})

outputs.label: VI-
outputs.formula: sum(abs(low - high[1]), {length}) / sum(max(high - low, max(abs(high - close[1]), abs(low - close[1]))), {length})

published.says: +VM = |high - prior low|; -VM = |low - prior high|; TR = max(high - low, |high - prior close|, |low - prior close|); +VI = n-period sum of +VM / n-period sum of TR; -VI likewise.
published.note: Length 14 follows StockCharts; other sources suggest 21.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for.

outputs.label: Choppiness Index
outputs.formula: 100 * log10(sum(max(high - low, max(abs(high - close[1]), abs(low - close[1]))), {length}) / (highest(high, {length}) - lowest(low, {length}))) / log10({length})

published.says: 100 x LOG10(SUM(ATR(1), n) / (MaxHi(n) - MinLo(n))) / LOG10(n); length 14.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for.

published.says: Bull Power = high - 13-period EMA of the close; Bear Power = low - the same EMA.
published.note: TradingView's built-in 'Bull Bear Power' plots the SUM of the two as one line; this entry is Elder's two lines.

capture.detail: TradingView draws ONE line, bull power plus bear power; the sum of this entry's two lines equals it on every bar.

outputs.label: Squeeze on
outputs.formula: sma(close, {bb_length}) - {bb_mult} * stdev(close, {bb_length}) > sma(close, {kc_length}) - {kc_mult} * sma(max(high - low, max(abs(high - close[1]), abs(low - close[1]))), {kc_length}) && sma(close, {bb_length}) + {bb_mult} * stdev(close, {bb_length}) < sma(close, {kc_length}) + {kc_mult} * sma(max(high - low, max(abs(high - close[1]), abs(low - close[1]))), {kc_length})

sources.title: The script's source as its author posted it

published.says: Bollinger band: 20-bar simple average of the close, 2 standard deviations. Keltner channel: the same average, 1.5 x the 20-bar simple average of the true range. Squeeze on = both Bollinger bands inside the Keltner channel. Momentum = linear regression (20) of close - average of (the 20-bar highest high and lowest low midpoint, the 20-bar average close).
published.note: This is LazyBear's public formula, named as his. John Carter's TTM Squeeze as he published it was not confirmed on a page read, so 'TTM Squeeze' is not a name in this library.

sources.title: StockCharts ChartSchool: Double Exponential Moving Average (DEMA)

published.says: EMA1 = EMA(price, n); EMA2 = EMA(EMA1, n); DEMA = 2 x EMA1 - EMA2. Mulloy, Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, January 1994.
published.note: Length 9 is TradingView's default; StockCharts uses 20.

sources.title: StockCharts ChartSchool: Triple Exponential Moving Average (TEMA)

published.says: EMA1 = EMA(price); EMA2 = EMA(EMA1); EMA3 = EMA(EMA2), one period; TEMA = 3 x EMA1 - 3 x EMA2 + EMA3.
published.note: Length 9 is TradingView's default; StockCharts uses 20.

outputs.label: Chande Momentum Oscillator
outputs.formula: 100 * (sum(max(close - close[1], 0), {length}) - sum(max(close[1] - close, 0), {length})) / (sum(max(close - close[1], 0), {length}) + sum(max(close[1] - close, 0), {length}))

sources.title: TradingView help center: Chande Momentum Oscillator
Fidelity learning center: Chande Momentum Oscillator

published.says: CMO = 100 x (Su - Sd) / (Su + Sd): Su is the sum of the close-to-close gains over the period, Sd the sum of the losses (as positive numbers). Plain sums; no smoothing.
published.note: Length 9 is TradingView's built-in default; its help page and Fidelity say 20 is usual.

sources.title: TradingView help center: Stochastic RSI (STOCH RSI)

published.says: StochRSI = (RSI - lowest RSI) / (highest RSI - lowest RSI) over the lookback (Chande and Kroll, The New Technical Trader, 1994). TradingView draws it 0 to 100 as K, a 3-bar simple average of that, and D, a 3-bar simple average of K.
published.note: The original is one line from 0 to 1 with no smoothing; this is TradingView's K and D form, 0 to 100.

held.name: Pocket Pivot
held.why: The authors' own rules page states the volume rule only. Whether the day must itself be an up day, and how a down-volume day is defined, were not confirmed on a page read. UCT's own readers (the Screener's Bar Character, Chart IQ) use 'an up day on more volume than any down day of the prior 10'; a chart formula should be proved equal to that before it is offered under the name.
held.describe: an up day on more volume than any down day of the last 10 days

held.name: TTM Squeeze
held.why: John Carter's own formula was not confirmed on a page read; the sources that describe it disagree about the channel's range. The Squeeze Momentum Indicator is in the library under its own author's name.
held.describe: the Bollinger Bands inside the Keltner Channels

held.name: Mansfield Relative Strength
held.why: The Screener has a column of this name. A chart formula for it belongs with the Screener's columns (chart_twins), proved equal to that column; until then there is no checked chart formula.
